nodes.label: Cash distributions are measured, not corrected either, and unlike a split the amount is known -- so a payout withholds only the criteria it actually decided rather than the whole reading. Both questions are asked against one series with every print on one scale, and asked in that order. First the structure: a session before an ex-date can outprint the top the stock actually made, so the tops are re-found on that series and the whole structure's boundaries are compared, not just the peak -- and whether the segmentation confirms that peak at all, because the ex-date drop is a retracement nobody traded and can be the very fall that confirms it -- a payout can leave the top exactly where it was and still move where the advance started, how long it took and which forty sessions the volume was measured against, and any of those moving leaves nothing here deciding. Then the answers, reading by reading, because a structure surviving does not make its answers survive with it: the cash comes out of the prints between the anchor and the peak, so ninety-nine percent on the tape is a hundred and a half on one scale, every boundary matches, and which side of the limit that lands on is the whole verdict. A criterion that answers differently on the two scales is withheld under the payout's own name; an ordinary quarterly payment is a fraction of a percent against a twenty-five percent limit and moves nothing. Per reading rather than pooled across the chain: the tops sit at different sessions, so a longer flag holds payouts a shorter one never saw, and a reading whose answer the payout decided abstains rather than disputes. What was paid is reported beside the structure in two figures, split at the flag's low: cash paid on or before the low came out of the price that made that low, cash paid after it did not, and a reader auditing a withheld criterion needs to see which. A history that does not carry the distribution column has not said there were none, and that absence is its own gap, the same as a missing split column. What is reported stays on the prints the tape made -- the peak, the anchor, the durations, the depths and the volume spans are the printed ones, and the one-scale series decides only what those numbers are allowed to settle, never what they are.

The provider supplies the split events and the prices stay the ones the tape printed, so a split inside the measured span -- which runs back through the volume baseline, not just the structure -- leaves nothing here deciding, in the verdict channel and in the signals alike. nodes.label: The base's left edge is where the stock last broke out of a structure and stayed out -- a close above a prior high, before the pivot formed, on volume above its own preceding fifty sessions, with every low since above that high. Where the base begins is read three ways -- not bounded at all, bounded where holding admits no reset, and bounded where a shallow failure that recovered still counts as leaving -- and a base is proposed only where all three agree. Each reading is defensible and each is wrong somewhere: strict holding misses a departure the source would recognise, tolerant holding cuts at a marginal one, and no boundary lets a structure the stock has left lend a contraction to the one above it. Picking any of them reached ready on a chain the detector had edited, once by deleting the contraction that widened and once by borrowing one. That is the source's own buy point, and it is the observation price alone does not supply: on price a rally above an earlier rally top inside a correction and a fresh consolidation under an old peak are the same picture at different magnitudes. A segmentation that neighbouring multiples disagree with is not proposed at all, and neither is one where any run in the sweep could not order a session inside the base: two runs that lost the same evidence agree on every anchor date without either having found anything, which is not agreement. The disagreement, or the session, is returned instead. Most real histories come back that way, because real price structure has no single canonical scale, and an unsettled segmentation is the honest answer rather than a defect to tune away.

nodes.label: The Power Play spans are drawn too, and they are the questions ticker.power-play raises from this history rather than a structure this capability picked out for itself. That capability cannot settle the volume clause alone -- the source says an explosive move commences on huge volume and names no number -- so it issues a chart question per undecided criterion per candidate top and waits, and each question carries the whole span it is about. Read here with nothing answered, because answers live in a request and this capability is not in it: the picture is what a reader is asked before they answer, and a span they have since settled is drawn again rather than dropped. The picture shows, for every open question, the anchor the advance is measured from, the peak it ended on, the flag low, the quiet window the volume ratio was divided by, and the heaviest session of the advance -- as far as the question named them. That anchor is the last quiet session and the advance is read from the one after it, so the rule is labelled as beginning the move after the session it stands on rather than on it: a session's difference lands on exactly the judgment a reader opens this picture to make. A history ending on the peak has no flag low and one beginning inside the advance has no baseline, and a landmark the question did not carry is not on the picture. Each artifact reports what it drew one list per landmark, so a mark that is absent because nothing named it is distinguishable from one absent because this timeframe does not reach the session. A chain read to several tops is usually one advance, so a landmark is drawn once per bar it falls on and carries the dates of every reading that landed there, only where the readings actually differ. Counted per bar rather than per date because a weekly bar holds a week of them: deduped by date, five tops drew five stars at three positions with five legend entries behind them. The key is on no picture and never will be, so the legend's date is all a reader has to carry a mark back to the question it belongs to -- and at five entries over three marks it carried nothing. A mark that stands for more than one reading sits where that bar's readings reached -- the highest of the tops, the lowest of the flag lows -- and prints no volume multiple where they divided by different baselines. Every value comes from the question, so the two cannot describe different tops with the same digest on both -- which is what happened when this capability measured its own: it drew the highest top while the question was about a lower one, and the seam accepted the answer. The ratio is printed only where the bars are sessions -- the daily panel and the span panel: it divides one session's volume by a session baseline, and a weekly bar is five of them added together, so the weekly marks which week holds that session and states no multiple. Every other weekly label carries the same qualification, because the bar a mark stands on there is a week and not the session the question is keyed on: the rule names the session the advance begins after rather than calling that bar it, and the shade names the weeks holding the window's first and last sessions rather than the window -- a boundary session's week is one bar, so the rectangle covers sessions the window ended before and only the label can say so. The baseline it divides by is that window's median, and the median is drawn across the shaded window on those same panels, because it is the one number on the panel a reader cannot point at: shown the shade alone, the eye compares the marked session with the tallest bar inside it, and on a quiet window holding one enormous day a session marked ten times the baseline is visibly shorter than a bar in the shade. The legend names the median rather than the window for the same reason. Where there is a span, a third picture holds it: the sessions from a week before the quiet window through the last bar, and no more -- the lead-in so that window's left edge is visible as an edge rather than as the side of the page. Up to a week, since a history beginning inside its own baseline has no sessions to give: the panel then starts where the history does, and that edge is the side of the page because there is nothing before it to draw. Three years of history is seven hundred sessions in twelve inches, and a four-session flag there is a few pixels under a marker wider than the flag -- a reader asked whether that flag corrected no more than a quarter was looking at something they could not measure. The two whole-history pictures are what a base is read from and are unchanged; this one is where the flag and the volume ratio are judged, and it draws no moving averages, because an average over one span is not the one the daily panel draws at the same dates. Nothing is drawn when nothing is being asked, and this capability holds no opinion about whether a structure deserves the question. The overlay names its own input beside itself, in power_play.measured_bars: input_sha256 covers the five price columns, which identifies the candles but not this overlay, since a split or a payout inside a span changes which questions exist without touching a price. Two histories differing only there once produced two questions and a chart with no span at all, digests matching on both, and the answer read off that blank picture was accepted. It is null where the history did not carry both kinds of event -- splits and distributions alike, since a payout inside a span withdraws criteria a split would leave undecided -- and a history missing either one is one no question is issued from.
